summary: Open. This is de Weger's conjecture with everything proved removed from its scope: no binomial collision C(n,k) = C(m,l) (2 ≤ k ≤ n/2, 2 ≤ l ≤ m/2, k < l) exists whose pair (k,l) is outside the nine solved ones, which is not of the adjacent shape (n−1,k+1), and which has n > 10^6. (Also known and consistent, but not usable as holes because they are pure non-existence statements: no collisions of the shapes (n−1,k+2), (n−2,k+1) [Stroeker–de Weger 1999] and none with C(n,k) ≤ 10^60 [BBdW §2.2].) The only general tool is Siegel's theorem, which gives finiteness pair by pair, ineffectively; a bound uniform in (k,l) is what Singmaster's conjecture needs and nothing published supplies it.
